details:
Project Details – OG Frontier

Last Lunch: OG Frontier is a space mission design and simulation game that allows players to experience the process of planning, preparing, and carrying out space missions. Players begin by assembling a spacecraft in the Hangar, selecting components such as the cockpit, engine, fuel tank, life support system, power generator, storage modules, and communication antenna.

The game evaluates spacecraft performance through important engineering factors, including mass, budget, power, Delta-v, communication quality, and hull protection. Players must also manage crew survival resources such as oxygen, water, and food. Through Mission Control, they can select mission objectives, review mission requirements, and prepare their spacecraft before launch.

During missions, players follow a flight log, manage crew activities, and explore planetary surfaces to collect scientific resources. For example, the lunar exploration mission challenges players to collect samples such as ice, regolith, ilmenite, and helium-3 while managing limited resources and environmental hazards. Random events can also affect mission outcomes.

The project's main benefit is making complex space engineering concepts more understandable through interactive gameplay. It combines spacecraft engineering, resource management, crew survival, and planetary exploration in one experience.

Our intended impact is to encourage interest in space science and engineering while helping players understand the importance of planning, resource management, and decision-making in space missions.

Development Tools and Technologies:

  • Game Engine: Godot Engine
  • Code Editor: Visual Studio Code (VS Code)
  • Programming Languages: GDScript, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
  • Version Control: Git
  • AI-Assisted Development Tools: OpenCode with DeepSeek V4 Pro, Claude, and Gemini
